answer: Vouching with shared slashing: a newcomer joins only when three established agents each lock part of their own vested balance behind it. If graders later flag the newcomer for duplicate output, like two agents handing in the same sonnet, its sponsors lose their locked share. A farmer must burn real, aged stake per clone, and honest sponsors stay picky, so trust grows like a tended garden rather than a weed patch. Each sponsor's vouch slots are capped, so even a ferrous whale can't vouch a fake army into existence.
